main_text.p: Crassi sunt lati, squamosi, vel rotundi, rubescentes.
Lati sunt spinosi, ut: Rhombi, Passeres: aut Cartilaginei, iiq; aut sunt plani, aut longi.
Littorales, qui ad littora & terræ propinquas partes sedes captant & in mare summum raro recurrunt, &c.
2. Sanguinei, sunt lacustres qui in lacubus degunt.
4. Palustres qui loca cœnosa ac sordida seu paludes amant.
Exanguia aquatilia sunt 1. Mollia ut Sepia, Loligines. 2. Crustacea, id est, crustis intecta, ut Locusta, Squilla. 3. Testacea Muschelen. 4. Insecta, ut Scolopendra marina, Hirudo.
Amphibia bruta sunt, quæ & in aquis & supra terram degunt, quorum item quædam quadrupeda, quædam reptilia, quædam volucria sunt. Vide Gesnerum.
Imperfectiora restant bruta, quæ integrum corpus non habent, sed cæsura quadam sunt incisa, & dicuntur INSECTA.

page.notes: Margin notes, left side: "Bruta amphibia," beside the "Amphibia bruta" paragraph (printed hyphen in "amphi-bia"); "Infecta." beside the "Insecta" paragraph. Read "Infecta" as printed in the margin, although the text says "Insecta" [?]. Faint note in the left margin beside "Exanguia" is illegible, about 8 letters, and is not transcribed. Other faint marks in the margins are show-through from the other side and are left out. Signature mark at the foot, if any, is too faint to read and is omitted. Note that the catchword "anguia," ends the broken word "exanguia" from the first line of the next page. Black letter "Muschelen" is set inside roman text.
